title: chemdisco: an auditable drug-discovery pipeline with provenance by construction
description:
A computational drug-discovery pipeline whose output is its own audit trail. Curated ChEMBL bioactivity data, QSAR validated on scaffold splits against a random-split baseline, fragment-based generation constrained to a measured anchoring motif, and Vina docking used as a filter rather than a ranking.

Every quantity carries its origin (measured, derived, predicted or heuristic) and provenance degrades rather than upgrades through the pipeline. A check that cannot discriminate is withheld and says so: the triage threshold is reported, not applied, because no candidate cleared it by more than the docking method's own error. An empty or unranked result is reported as a result.

What the archived runs establish: cross-machine reproduction of a prior run's ligand and curation signatures, and one conclusion reached by three independent routes (redocking, enrichment at doubled search effort, and a 5x5 cross-docking matrix) that on this target the limit is the scoring function rather than the sampling. This is verified reproduction and enforced provenance. It is not a discovery.

Code is MIT. Derived data under runs/ inherits ChEMBL's CC BY-SA 3.0 -- see DATA_LICENSE.md.
